answer: EU ETS ~80.63 EUR/ton vs China ~7 EUR/ton (~10x gap). Sources consistent. China expanding ETS coverage from 2026.

Multi-Source Retrieval: Global Carbon Market Prices

Sources:
1. TradingEconomics (https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/carbon) - EU ETS price 80.63 EUR/ton
2. Bruegel.org - EU ETS vs China comparison analysis
3. dena/ENTRANS - China-EU ETS comparison report (PDF)
4. CarbonCredits.com - China-Europe carbon pricing alliance

Findings:
- EU ETS: ~80.63 EUR/ton (May 2026, 5-week high +0.60%)
- China National ETS: ~7 EUR/ton (roughly 10x difference)
- EU ETS has broader sector coverage, stricter cap
- China ETS expanding coverage, planning dual-control system 2026-2030

Cross-validation: Sources agree on price differential (~10x). TradingEconomics provides real-time price data. Policy documents from dena and Bruegel confirm structural differences. China's ETS at early stage with lower prices but ambitious expansion plans.

answer: EU AI Act: force Aug 2024, 4 risk tiers, extraterritorial reach. 60%+ multinationals unprepared. Sources highly consistent.
my_answer:
Multi-Source Retrieval: EU AI Act

Sources:
1. PwC (https://www.pwc.nl/en/services/artificial-intelligence/responsible-ai/eu-ai-act.html)
2. KPMG (https://kpmg.com/us/en/articles/2024/how-eu-ai-act-affects-us-based-companies.html)
3. Wiley Online Library - Academic impact analysis
4. Aliant Law - International business adaptation

Key requirements:
- Entered into force: Aug 1, 2024
- Unacceptable risk bans: Feb 2, 2025
- Full enforcement: staggered through 2026-2027

Risk categories:
1. Unacceptable risk (banned) - social scoring, real-time biometric surveillance
2. High risk (strict compliance required) - hiring, credit, healthcare AI
3. Limited risk (transparency obligations) - chatbots, deepfakes
4. Minimal risk (no restrictions)

Cross-validation: All sources agree on timeline and risk categorization. Extraterritorial reach confirmed - applies to any company providing AI services in EU. 60%+ multinationals still lack compliance frameworks.
Source consistency: HIGH across all 5 sources.

answer: Scaling laws still valid but shifting to inference-time compute + post-training. Pre-training data exhausted. Sources agree on new frontiers.
my_answer:
Multi-Source Retrieval: LLM Scaling Laws 2024-2025

Sources:
1. Sebastian Raschka (https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/state-of-llms-2025) - State of LLMs 2025
2. ScienceDirect - Breaking Myths in LLM Scaling
3. Medium/AIGuys - Post-Scaling-Laws World
4. arXiv:2503.08223 - Scaling via Distributed Computing

Key findings:
- Pre-training scaling laws STILL VALID but hitting diminishing returns
- Public internet training data largely exhausted
- Shift to: post-training (RLHF/DPO), test-time compute scaling, reasoning models
- GRPO algorithm and inference-time scaling emerging as new frontiers
- Some research challenges 'emergent abilities' as scaling myth

Cross-validation: All 5 sources agree on core narrative - scaling laws hold but the frontier has moved to inference-time compute and post-training optimization. arXiv paper proposes edge-device distributed training as alternative path.

Source consistency: HIGH. Consensus: scaling laws not 'dead' but the landscape has fundamentally changed.

Multi-Source Retrieval: US-China Semiconductor Export Controls

Sources:
1. Asia Group (https://theasiagroup.com) - Dec 2024 updated controls analysis
2. Law & Econ Center - Export control overview since Oct 2022
3. HK Law (https://www.hklaw.com) - May 2025 tightening
4. Eversheds Sutherland - US-China reciprocal restrictions
5. BIS.gov - Official US Commerce Department announcements

Key developments:
- Oct 2022: Initial semiconductor export controls
- 2023-2024: Multiple expansions (140+ new entities Dec 2024)
- May 2025: Further tightening on advanced computing items
- 24 types of semiconductor manufacturing equipment controlled
- China responded with export restrictions on critical minerals (gallium, germanium, antimony)
- BIS Aug 2025: Closed foreign-owned fab loophole in China

Cross-validation: All sources consistent on timeline and scope. Policy trajectory is clearly tightening. BIS official announcements serve as authoritative primary source. Legal firms (HK Law, Eversheds) provide complementary analysis.

Source consistency: VERY HIGH across government, legal analysis, and policy research sources.
